candidates.term: The Magistrate inside the Month Gate
candidates.defline: The Magistrate holds your strongest seat, inside your Month Gate: your working years are built on duty done properly.
candidates.reading: You feel most yourself when you have a clear role and do it well, and your working years are shaped around that need. Because steady reliability earns trust, your responsibilities grow year by year inside the places you join. The frame that supports you also holds you in, and your freedom shrinks as your rank grows. Your influence comes from being dependable, and it is greater than it looks.
candidates.teaser: Your prime is built for responsibility: the frame of your working life is duty done properly. Titles find you midlife, and they tend to stick.

domain_readings.Career: Duty done properly is the frame of your working life: your growth compounds inside institutions the way interest compounds inside banks. Midlife hands you titles that stay. The deep cost is elasticity. Renegotiate your role every few years on purpose. Structure serves best reviewed.
domain_readings.Growth: You grow inside frameworks and outgrow them on schedule: each structure teaches, then confines, then hands you to the next. Honor the rhythm. The promotion beyond a frame is also a form of loyalty to it. Climb without guilt.
domain_readings.Social: People organize around your steadiness: teams stabilize, committees function, chaos finds its filing system. Your influence wears reliability’s plain clothes. Know exactly what that is worth. The one who keeps things standing quietly decides what stands.

candidates.life_chapter: Your rising chapter builds inside great structures: the prime decades build inside structures, and the structures build you back, title by title. Expect your steadiness to become the department’s foundation. Review the building every few years. Foundations deserve architects, not just tenants.
candidates.relations: The org chart neighbors are this seat’s people: reports who trust you, seniors who rely on you, the whole scaffolding of working bonds. They will define these decades’ friendships. Take two of them beyond the building. Colleagues age into brothers if invited.
candidates.turn_catalyst: Run thin, the frame stays theoretical: capability unenrolled. Join the structure worth your decade this year. The engine needs a building.
candidates.turn_friction: Run heavy, the institution becomes the identity: the badge outranking the man. Spend one weekend monthly as nobody’s title.
candidates.shadow_line: Overloaded, the frame holds you more than up: security renamed confinement.
candidates.health_line: Your health runs on office rhythm: regular hours suit you biologically. Guard the weekends from the weekdays, and both improve.

Career.headline: Your career grows steadily inside a structure.
Career.recognition: You do your best work inside an organisation with fixed rules and a visible ladder, and you climb it by doing every step properly. Because you need to know where you stand, open-ended jobs leave you uneasy, and a proper title settles you. What you gain is lasting rank, and what you lose is the freedom to move quickly.
Career.lived: Since your late teens your career has moved up in steady steps, a promotion earned or a responsibility added each time you proved yourself. Your seniors noticed your reliability early, and you were trusted with more than your age suggested.

Growth.headline: You grow by moving from one structure to the next.
Growth.recognition: You grow inside a framework, a course or a firm or a discipline, until you have learned everything it can teach. Because loyalty runs deep in you, leaving one structure for a bigger one feels like a betrayal, and you wait longer than you need to. Your growth comes in clear stages, and each one starts when you finally move.
Growth.lived: From your late teens you grew through formal steps, a qualification finished or a rank reached or a role handed over to you. Each structure you joined shaped you for a few years, and you outgrew most of them on time.

Social.headline: People rely on you to keep things steady.
Social.recognition: You are the one who keeps a group working, the colleague who remembers the deadline and the friend who makes the plan happen. Because order calms you, you take on the organising without being asked, and people come to depend on it. Your place in a circle is quiet, and you decide more than anyone credits you for.
Social.lived: Since your late teens your friendships have grown out of work and shared duties, the colleagues you trusted and the seniors who trusted you. You became the steady one in every group you joined, and some of those bonds have lasted well beyond the job.
